newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovakia says US criticism on reforms unfair - TASR.
newsitem.headline: Slovakia says US criticism on reforms unfair - TASR.

text.p: Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik on Monday hit back at the U.S. for criticising the pace of democratic reforms in Slovakia, saying it was progressing in the same direction as its neighbours.

Hamzik, referring to his visit to Washington last week, said comments made by Secretary of State Madeleine Albright that Slovakia was foot-dragging in democratic reforms were unfair and not justified.
"I cannot agree with those who seek to portray Slovakia as a problematic country," Hamzik told the official news agency TASR.

"A lot of work in both political and economic reform has been done (in Slovakia) over the last eight years," Hamzik said, adding that Slovakia has been developing a market economy on a democratic basis.

The U.S. and several European Union countries have several times expressed disappointment with the pace of reforms in the areas of media freedom and minorities issues in Slovakia since it became independent in 1993.

The Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland have been lauded for their reforms following the collapse of Communism in 1989, and are considered front-runners to be invited to join the NATO security alliance as well as the EU.
Slovakia has said also it wants to join NATO in its first wave of eastward expansion, but its chances appear to have waned.
Slovakia, which currently holds associate EU membership, applied in 1995 for full EU membership.
